content: MPL-2.0 (whatsmeow's license) is weak copyleft: file-level, not project-level. Obligations trigger ONLY when distributing the Covered Software itself (source or modified source) — you must keep copyright headers/notices and make your modifications to MPL files available under MPL-2.0. A 'Larger Work' combining MPL files with your own separate files may be under terms of your choice; new files containing no MPL-licensed code are NOT Modifications and need not be MPL even in a Larger Work. Private use (inside an organization) creates no obligations at all. Key implication for sdk-wa: if no whatsmeow code is copied, a clean .NET reimplementation under e.g. MIT/Apache-2.0 has no MPL obligation — but the hygiene must be real: no verbatim copying, no mechanical translation, no pasting of MPL-licensed code with headers stripped (that IS distributing Covered Software / a Modification). Protocol facts, wire formats, and behavior are not copyrightable expression in the same way, but the arrangement/structure of copied code is. Also note: MPL 2.0 is compatible with GPL as a Secondary License combination. Recommend: written clean-room policy, no code-level diffing sessions, cite protocol behavior not code, document provenance. This is not legal advice.
